name: Whiteface Mountain
operator: New York State Olympic Regional Development Authority (ORDA)

source.note: Piste reference data (not web-verified in this build) — confirm at source. Approximate main base-lodge position off NY-86 south-west of Wilmington

Official stats: base 1,220 ft; vertical 3,430 ft (greatest in the East, includes hike-to terrain; 3,166 ft lift-serviced). Summit stored as base + vertical (~4,650 ft, top of hike-to terrain); the mountain peak is 4,867 ft (1,483 m).

Official Mountain Stats page via search summary (2026-10-03): 94 trails; 299 skiable acres plus 35 acres of in-bounds off-piste double-black terrain on The Slides; lifts: 1 eight-passenger gondola, 2 high-speed detachable quads, 3 fixed quads, 1 triple, 2 doubles and 2 conveyors (= 11).

character: A state-owned Adirondack ski mountain near Lake Placid, run by ORDA, with one of the largest vertical drops in the eastern US and steep, often wind-exposed upper terrain. It hosted the alpine events of the 1980 Winter Olympics.
learning: Reference note: beginner terrain and lessons are concentrated at the Bear Den area near the main base, away from the steep upper mountain. Confirm current learning lifts and lesson programs.

season.notes: No official 2026-27 opening or closing date found as of 2026-10-03. OnTheSnow projects Nov 21, 2026 (third-party projection, not an announcement). ORDA typically announces opening dates in November (2025-26 dates were announced 2025-11-21).
